coverage_notes:
SOURCES USED. (1) Wikipedia 1999 Florida State Seminoles football team page (has a 13-row coaching-staff table). (2) The school's own athletics site archived in-season on the Wayback Machine: the "Florida State Staff Roster" page captured 1999-11-18 (11 names) plus each coach's individual 1999 bio page captured Oct 1999 - Mar 2000. (3) The official 1999 Florida State Football Media Guide, scanned in full on the Internet Archive (item florida-state-football-1999-media-guide, 278 scanned pages) - this is what unlocked the support tiers: printed p. 44 (strength staff), p. 46 "FOOTBALL STAFF" (equipment + graduate assistants), p. 47 "TRAINING STAFF", p. 48 "SUPPORT STAFF" photo grid. (4) Contemporary/retrospective bios for corroboration (ESU Warriors for Demarest, FSU Athletics Hall of Fame for Oravetz, Wikipedia for Gabbard).

WHAT IS FULLY RECOVERED. Head coach; all 9 on-field assistants (Amato, Andrews, J. Bowden, Gladden, Haggins, Heggins, Lilly, Richt, Sexton); the strength and conditioning coach; both football graduate assistants; the five strength and conditioning graduate assistants; both equipment managers; the sports medicine director and the two assistant trainers assigned to football; and the entire 20-person "SUPPORT STAFF" grid (physicians, dentist, optometrist, chiropractor, security, video, chaplain, dietician, dorm supervisor, and the recruiting/secretarial/football-operations staff). Total 43 people.

WHAT I COULD NOT RECOVER, PLAINLY. (a) ANALYST and QUALITY CONTROL tiers: none exist. Those job categories did not exist at FSU in 1999 under then-current NCAA staff limits, and the media guide lists no such positions. Zero rows in those categories is a real finding, not a gap. (b) Randy Oravetz's bio states he "leads a staff of six full-time assistant trainers and a large group of student trainers" - only the two with football-specific duties (Duane Brooks, David Walls) are named individually anywhere I could find. The other four full-time assistant trainers are undocumented by name. (c) Student managers are referenced in aggregate ("A large staff of student managers, supervised by Callaway") but never named. Same for student athletic trainers. (d) Football-specific academic support staff are not listed in the football media guide and I found no archived athletics-department staff directory from 1999-2000 (the seminoles.com/genrel captures contain no staff directory).

QUOTE CAVEATS. The 1999 media guide exists only as an image scan. For people whose auto-OCR transcription is faithful I cite the Internet Archive's plain-text OCR file (_djvu.txt) with the exact OCR string, and flag in the note that the string is OCR (some words are misrendered, e.g. "Asistont", "ffh"). For the printed p. 48 SUPPORT STAFF photo grid the OCR interleaves the grid's five columns and corrupts several names (it renders "MARK RODIN" as "MARK Croom" and merges "DR. DOUG HENDERSON"/"DR. KRIS STOWERS" into "DR. KRIS HENDERSON"), and it drops "DEBRA CREWS" and "RANDY ORAVETZ" entirely - so for those rows I set quote to "" per instruction and read the name and title directly off the page image. Every such row was visually verified at high resolution against the original scan; none are inferred.

RING-RULE EDGE CASE. Chuck Amato was named NC State's head coach on January 6, 2000 - two days AFTER the January 4, 2000 Sugar Bowl. He coached the championship game as FSU's assistant head coach, so he is a full-season, championship-game member of the staff. No other arrivals or departures during the 1999 season were documented, so no row carries a midseason_note.

ROLE-WORDING NOTE. Where sources word a role differently I used the school's own in-season staff roster wording and recorded the variant in the source note (e.g. Odell Haggins is "Defensive Line" on the staff roster and in the media guide header but "Defensive Tackles" in the Position field of his own bio page; John Lilly is "Tight Ends/Recruiting Coordinator" on the roster and "Tight Ends/ Recruiting Coordinator" on his bio).
